the genetics of human NK cells in health and disease and with their roles in immunity and reproduction.

NK cell mediated immunity is an essential component of human immune responses to pathogens and that NK cell mediated plentation is an essential component in human reproduction.
HLA A, HLA B, HLA C, and KIR genes are in linkage disequilibrium with each other in the general population, and the HLA class I and KIR gene frequencies differ among ethnic populations.
NK cell genetics is a complex and rapidly evolving system that is essential in human health, disease, and survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic diversity of NK cells in human populations and species of higher primates is a result of natural selection by pathogens, and by constraints on NK cell mediated reproduction.
the genetics of NK cells in human health, disease and survival is the result of the interaction between NK cell mediated immunity to pathogens and NK cell mediated placental function.
the genetics of human NK cell receptors and ligands are complex but fascinating, and that the NK cells themselves are vital for human survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetics of NK cells is a major determinant of human health and survival, and that the genetics of HLA and killer cell immunoglobulins is a major determinant for this.
the genetic diversity of NK cell receptors and HLA class I ligands has profound effects on human survival and health.
the NK cell mediated immune response is an important determinant of human health and survival.
